This is now a 6-day-old pattern, not noise: worth an actual fix (allowlist the price-data domains in this environment's network policy, or move the routine to a source that's already allowlisted) rather than hoping it clears on its own. One more thing worth flagging: there's no daily-check commit in the repo for Aug 27 at all — that day may have failed to run entirely rather than just losing its price feed. No live prices today; P&L, stop/TP proximity, and exit-strategy checks below are skipped rather than estimated, per the skill's own "N/A is better than wrong" rule. Both open positions already carry IBKR-side GTC stop orders and email alerts (GOOG ≤$333.90, SPXC ≤$186.90) that work independently of this report — check the IBKR app directly for current levels.

No watchlist name is live enough to fund with freed cash once it lands; that's a job for stock-finder when there's a candidate.

📚 Today you learned

Non-Operating Gains — Reading Through a One-Time Mark in EPS

CRM's headline today — adjusted EPS of $5.90 vs. $3.27 consensus, an 80%+ beat — is the kind of number that moves a stock 20%+ in a session, and it did. But roughly $2.6B of that beat was a mark-to-market gain on Salesforce's equity stake in Anthropic (whose private valuation jumped), not cash from selling more CRM software. Revenue only grew a normal 11% YoY, in line with estimates. This is the SBC/adjusted-EBITDA lesson again in a new costume: "adjusted" earnings often exclude the messy stuff going one direction (stock comp) while including favorable one-time marks going the other. The test is always the same — strip the non-recurring item and ask if the operating business alone still clears the bar. Here it barely does; the stock move mostly priced a paper gain that reverses if Anthropic's valuation cools.

Also today: Strategic equity stake — when an operating company holds shares in a private or public partner (often a customer or AI infra partner) as a side investment; gains/losses on it show up in "other income," not core operations.

Research output, not financial advice. Past performance does not guarantee future results.
